findings.description: All concurrent or nested invocations of the same wrapped function now share and clear a single statistics dict. Previously each call got its own copy's statistics.
findings.rationale: Trigger: two threads (or recursive calls) invoke the same decorated function at once. Each call runs stats.clear() and then writes into the same dict. One call resets the other's attempt_number and start_time mid-run, so the statistics are corrupted. If the retry logic reads the stats (for example attempt_number for stop conditions), retry behavior can be wrong as well.

findings.description: Async wrapper clears and shares one statistics dict across all concurrent calls of the same decorated coroutine.
findings.rationale: Trigger: asyncio.gather of several calls to the same retry-decorated coroutine. Each call does stats.clear() and all of them write into the same dict, so attempt_number is reset or interleaved between tasks. The result is wrong statistics, and possibly wrong stop or wait decisions that depend on attempt_number.
